inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment charges' 129 (AAL.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:15567). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in every period). Awards are settled with market-purchased shares (US$106m bought in H1 2026, mostly for employee schemes), so the charge is cash-funded.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average ordinary shares for the six months to 30 June 2026 (1,080m; basic 1,072m), interim report note 5. Post the May 2025 share consolidation that accompanied the Valterra Platinum demerger. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and funded by on-market purchases. The Anglo Teck merger would issue new shares to Teck holders (Anglo holders to own c.62.4%) -- NOT modelled; this is a standalone valuation.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD; LSE quote in GBp (pence). GBPUSD 1.3157 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-11-18T15:52Z) => 1 USD = 76.005 GBp (100 / 1.3157). Parity check against the USD OTC ordinary line AAUKF: LSE pence price x 1.3157 / 100 ties to the AAUKF USD quote of the same hour within 0.1%, which confirms the rate, its direction and the pence basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T15:37:43Z (Yahoo chart API; an intraday LSE print on the last session before the valuation date, not a confirmed close -- replace at the next regular close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% nominal USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year risk-free c.4.3% + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta c.1.2 gives a cost of equity near 10.3%; c.15% debt weight at c.5.5% pre-tax brings WACC to c.9%. The asset base is Chile, Peru, South Africa and Brazil, but country and commodity risk are charged in the scenario flows (price decks, volumes, tax/royalty leakage) and the scenario weights, not as a WACC premium. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Company net debt of US$8,234m already includes lease liabilities of c.US$1,191m (it excludes US$306m of freight-index-priced variable vessel leases, which are an operating freight cost). Lease principal is therefore NOT deducted from the flows; ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged through the capex line (c.US$0.22bn a year on top of guided capex, against US$287m of FY2025 lease capital repayments for continuing operations including De Beers).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED tax-plus-minority leakage rate: c.40% underlying tax (long-term guidance for the simplified portfolio is 38-42%; mining royalties in Chile and Peru are inside it) and c.35% of post-tax operating profit to non-controlling interests (Mitsubishi 40% of Quellaveco, Codelco/Mitsui/Mitsubishi 49.9% of Anglo American Sur, c.47% of Sishen Iron Ore via Kumba and SIOC minorities; Collahuasi is a proportionately consolidated joint operation and Minas-Rio is 100% owned). 1 - 0.60 x 0.65 = 61%. Calibration: H1 2026 simplified-portfolio underlying EBIT 2,988 x 39% = 1,165 against attributable underlying earnings ex De Beers of 1,009 plus c.200 of attributable net finance cost; FY2025 4,822 x 39% = 1,881 against 1,646 plus c.450. No NCI deduction is made in the equity bridge. Minorities also fund their share of capex in excess of D&A, which this treatment charges 100% to Anglo holders -- a modest conservatism (c.US$0.1bn a year).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). A diversified miner's value is a stream of operating cash flow less sustaining capital; none of the non-FCF rows applies. First valuation of this ticker. SCOPE: the flows are the SIMPLIFIED PORTFOLIO only -- Copper, Premium Iron Ore, Manganese, Crop Nutrients, Corporate. FY2018-FY2024 history is the whole group (PGMs, coal, nickel, diamonds) and FY2025 onward is continuing operations including De Beers, so no historical series is extrapolated; base_revenue is FY2025 group revenue of 19,325 less De Beers 3,493 = 15,832 (segment note, AAL.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:15764), which is why it differs from the 18,546 statutory revenue on the Actuals sheet. De Beers (exiting, loss-making), Steelmaking Coal (sale to Dhilmar agreed) and Nickel (sale to MMG agreed) are valued in the equity bridge, not the flows -- every excluded stream has its asset in the bridge. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: revenue growth and margin paths are derived from an explicit commodity deck, not from the latest margin. Copper realised 623 c/lb for the first nine months of 2026 against 446 c/lb a year earlier; COMEX spot on the valuation date is c.566 c/lb. Base fades copper to 530 c/lb nominal by 2029 (c.US$5.00/lb in 2026 dollars) and holds it flat in real terms; bull holds c.US$6/lb real; bear falls to c.US$4/lb real. Volumes follow guidance (700-760 kt 2026, 750-810 kt 2027, 790-850 kt 2028). Premium iron ore at 59-61 Mt with EBITDA per tonne of US$36 base / US$45 bull / US$25 bear (H1 2026 US$38, FY2025 US$47). SBC: underlying EBITDA is struck after the share-based payment charge, so ebitda_margin_path is underlying EBITDA margin PLUS 0.7pp and the engine then deducts SBC once; house and street differ by only that 0.7% of revenue. INTEREST: net debt, so no interest income is stripped. last_fcf is the contract definition (statutory OCF - capex - SBC, continuing operations including De Beers and before minorities, leases and interest); the company's own attributable free cash flow was US$790m in FY2025 and US$803m in H1 2026 after interest, lease repayments and NCI distributions. BUYBACKS: cash spent is on-market purchases for employee schemes; no shareholder buyback programme is running. NOT MODELLED: the Anglo Teck merger (targeted completion by March 2027, China antitrust approval outstanding), its c.US$800m pre-tax synergies, and the c.US$4.5bn special dividend Anglo intends to pay its holders before completion (value-neutral standalone: cash out, net debt up). Woodsmith capex (c.US$0.25bn a year) is charged in the flows with no revenue or bridge value attributed. Manganese (40% of Samancor, equity-accounted) is carried at its proportionate revenue and EBITDA inside the flows, a small simplification.

equity_bridge.item: Steelmaking Coal + Nickel disposal groups at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Net assets held for sale US$2,352m at 30 June 2026 (coal 1,991 after the H1 2026 write-down to the Dhilmar sale terms; nickel 361), less the US$148m Dhilmar deposit already received and inside net debt = the 2,204 'capital employed related to disposal groups' in interim note 12. Price-linked contingent consideration (up to US$1.575bn) is carried at nil by the company and here.

equity_bridge.item: Discontinued operations cash burn to completion
equity_bridge.note: Coal and nickel consumed c.US$315m in H1 2026 before the deposit (operations -71, capex -149, leases -53, other). Completion expected Q1 2027; Moranbah North longwall ramp-up in Q3 2026 reduces the run-rate. Judgment.

equity_bridge.item: De Beers at 50% of attributable carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Capital employed US$2,300m at 30 June 2026 (interim note 12) x 85% Anglo share = 1,955, haircut 50%: the carrying value was set after the FY2025 US$2.3bn impairment, since when the consolidated realised price has fallen 37% and the price index 18%. Judgment -- no sale price has been announced.

equity_bridge.item: De Beers cash burn until sale
equity_bridge.note: Underlying EBITDA -113 in H1 2026 plus c.US$0.2bn a year of capex, 85% attributable, for roughly one year. Judgment.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle volume growth (c.1%) plus inflation; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every historical CAGR is a scope artefact, not a growth rate. FY2018-FY2024 is the whole group; FY2025 is continuing operations only (PGMs demerged May 2025, Steelmaking Coal and Nickel discontinued), and equity fell on c.US$10bn of impairments and the Valterra demerger. EPS is negative in FY2024 and FY2025, so no EPS CAGR exists. The equity CAGR diverges from the forward growth view by far more than 30% and is rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less share-based payment charge; no interest income stripped because the group carries net debt): FY2020 1,742, FY2022 3,230, FY2025 2,213. SBC is c.0.7% of revenue throughout, so the owner and reported series move together.

base.growth_rationale: Deck: copper 610/560/540 c/lb in 2026-28, 530 c/lb in 2029 (c.US$5.00 real) then +2% a year; copper production 725/780/820/830/850/870 kt then 880 kt; iron ore 59-61 Mt at c.US$105/t revenue; other revenue +2%. FY2026 simplified-portfolio revenue c.US$18.1bn and underlying EBITDA c.US$8.6bn against H1 actuals of 8.9bn and 4.1bn.
base.capex_rationale: Guided simplified-portfolio capex of c.US$3.0bn 2026, 2.9bn 2027, 2.6bn 2028, then US$2.5bn growing 2% (long-term sustaining guidance c.US$2.0bn ex life-extension, plus life-extension and volume growth), plus c.US$0.22bn a year of lease renewal.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined tax + minority-interest leakage, see inputs.nci_treatment.

bull.growth_rationale: Deck: copper 640 c/lb in 2027-28 and 645 c/lb in 2029 (c.US$6 real) then +2% a year; production to 920 kt by 2032 (Collahuasi debottlenecking and fourth line, Los Bronces-Andina joint mine plan from 2030); iron ore EBITDA c.US$44-45/t as the premium for high-grade product widens.
bull.capex_rationale: c.10% more capital than base in dollars to fund the higher copper volumes; lower as a share of the larger revenue base.

bear.growth_rationale: Deck: copper 510 c/lb in 2027, 450 in 2028, 430 in 2029 (c.US$4 real) then +2% a year; production stalls at 800 kt on Chilean water and permitting constraints; unit costs 5% above base; iron ore revenue c.US$92/t and EBITDA c.US$25/t as Simandou supply and weak Chinese steel demand compress the index.
bear.capex_rationale: Capital cut to c.US$2.4bn by 2029 (near the sustaining floor) but higher as a share of the smaller revenue base.
bear.cash_tax_rate_note: One point more leakage than base: royalty floors and unrelieved losses raise the effective rate when profits fall.

scenario_narratives.base: Copper comes off its 2026 highs and settles near US$5.00/lb in 2026 dollars, roughly the incentive price for new supply, while Anglo delivers the guided volume recovery to c.830 kt by 2029 as Collahuasi returns to higher-grade ore and the Los Bronces second plant runs, drifting to 880 kt in the 2030s. Premium iron ore holds 60 Mt with EBITDA per tonne near the H1 2026 level in nominal terms, a slow real decline as Simandou ramps. Underlying EBITDA settles around US$8bn (c.44% margin) against US$8.6bn in FY2026; capex falls from US$3.0bn to c.US$2.5bn. De Beers, coal and nickel exit at roughly carrying value for coal and nickel and half of carrying value for De Beers. The Teck merger is not in the numbers.
scenario_narratives.bull: The copper deficit thesis holds: electrification and data-centre demand against a decade of under-investment keep copper near US$6/lb in real terms, and Anglo's Chilean growth options (Collahuasi fourth line, Los Bronces-Andina joint plan) lift production past 900 kt. Steel decarbonisation widens the premium for Kumba lump and Minas-Rio pellet feed, taking iron ore EBITDA back to c.US$45/t. Underlying EBITDA reaches US$10-12bn at a margin above 50%. This case needs a sustained price above the incentive level for ten years plus clean execution in Chile; it still excludes Anglo Teck synergies.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese demand weakens and new supply arrives: copper retreats to c.US$4/lb real, Simandou and soft steel output push iron ore realisations down by more than 10%, and stronger producer currencies (rand, real, peso) lift unit costs. Chilean water and permitting problems -- the 2026 tribunal ruling on the Collahuasi desalination authorisation is the live example -- cap copper output at 800 kt. Underlying EBITDA falls to c.US$5bn (35% margin) and capex is cut to the sustaining floor. No scenario hits the zero terminal floor; the business remains cash-generative at US$4 copper, but with US$8.2bn of net debt the equity value falls by more than half from base.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the starting point is a copper price well above mid-cycle, iron ore faces a visible supply wave, and three disposals plus a merger are still open. Base 50%: copper near the incentive price with guided volumes is the central expectation. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs copper to hold c.US$6 real for a decade AND the Chilean expansions to be delivered, two things that must both go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Anglo American is valued as a standalone, simplified copper and premium iron ore producer on mid-cycle commodity prices, attributable to plc shareholders after a 61% combined tax-and-minority leakage, with the exiting businesses added at conservative disposal values. The market price capitalises something close to 2026 copper prices in perpetuity plus the Anglo Teck combination; this model does neither, so the gap between price and value is mostly a statement about the copper price and the merger, not about operating quality.
key_risks_to_valuation: Copper price: each US$0.50/lb on the long-run deck moves attributable owner FCF by roughly US$0.35bn a year. The bull-to-bear spread is almost entirely this one variable.

Anglo Teck merger (targeted by March 2027): excluded. Completion adds c.US$800m of pre-tax synergies shared 62.4/37.6, changes the share count and the asset mix, and comes with a c.US$4.5bn special dividend; this model must be rebuilt on a pro-forma basis when it closes.
De Beers exit value: carried at 50% of attributable carrying value. A sale at carrying value adds c.US$0.9/share; a nil-value exit with further cash burn removes about the same.

Minority and tax leakage: the 61% combined rate is calibrated to FY2025 and H1 2026. A higher copper share raises the minority share (Quellaveco, Anglo American Sur); Chilean and Peruvian royalty changes move the tax share.
Iron ore: Kumba depends on Transnet rail and port performance, and Simandou supply could compress both the index and the premium for high-grade product.

Terminal value: the 14x cap binds in the base case (Gordon at 9%/2% is 14.6x); mine lives are long but finite and sustaining capital is modelled at guidance, which excludes major life-extension projects.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2,639-4,643.8 GBp. FX from Yahoo GBPUSD=X, see inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: Anglo American Half Year Financial Report for the six months to 30 June 2026 (net debt, segment results, capex and tax guidance, held-for-sale note, diluted share count); Integrated Annual Report 2025 (FY2025 segment results, cash flow statement); Q3 2026 Production Report (realised prices, volumes, updated guidance); AAL.L_Metrics.csv for the FY2018-FY2025 history.
data_sources.qualitative: AAL.L_Analysis.json (portfolio simplification, Anglo Teck merger, De Beers, coal and nickel disposals, risk factors).
